comparison: Both evaluate the core structural work (C3, C32-C36) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides more comprehensive coverage including methodological claims (C37-C40) and structural inferences (C41-C43), while peer review focuses specifically on the quality and validity of the cryo-EM structure determination. Both affirm the structural work is solid and compelling.

Perfect alignment on claims C54-C61 regarding structural conservation and mechanistic insights. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative RMSD measurements and sequence alignment data, while peer review highlights the broader implications for understanding Hsp90-Cdc37 client diversity and plasticity.

Strong agreement on methodological claims (C75-C88). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed technical validation of each methodological step, while peer review acknowledges the engineered construct approach and affirms the methodology as 'state of the art.'

High concordance on background claims (C1-C2, C7-C28). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval characterizes these as well-established literature context, while peer review notes no concerns were raised about these foundational claims regarding mGC physiology and domain architecture.

Both address binding mechanism details (C44-C50) and evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes structural data from Figure 2 and quantitative PISA measurements, while peer review affirms the mechanistic similarity to kinase-chaperone interactions without raising concerns.

Significant disagreement on speculative regulatory models (C70-C74). OpenEval evaluates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are hypotheses lacking direct experimental support. Peer review evaluates as SUPPORTED, treating them as reasonable inferences that 'offer clues' about regulation. This represents a key difference in how speculative claims are assessed.

Both address the key finding that GC-C pseudokinase hijacks the kinase chaperone machinery (C4-C6). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes structural comparisons demonstrating conserved mechanisms, while peer review highlights this as the 'novelty of the work' and 'primary breakthrough.'

Both address previously proposed models and prior work (C62-C63, C65-C66). OpenEval evaluates as UNCERTAIN, noting the mechanistic model is speculative and requires validation. Peer review evaluates as SUPPORTED, accepting these as appropriate context without challenge. Difference reflects OpenEval's stricter assessment of speculative mechanistic claims.

Both address structural observations about asymmetric binding and missing density (C41-C43). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval characterizes these as reasonable inferences from structural data, while peer review implicitly accepts them through overall acceptance of structural findings.

Both address poorly resolved density and interface properties (C51-C53). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these are consistent with resolution limitations and mobility of unfolded regions, while peer review implicitly accepts resolution limitations and modeling approaches.

Both address sequence conservation between hamster and human proteins (C39-C40). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval validates this as part of methodological justification, while peer review implicitly accepts relevance of hamster proteins to human system.

Both address the engineered construct approach (C37-C38). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval validates these as appropriate methodological approaches, while peer review explicitly acknowledges the engineered construct and accepts the experimental design.

Both address quantitative interface measurement (C47). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate citation of PISA calculation method, while peer review accepts this as consistent with overall structural analysis without specific concerns.

Overlap on C59 regarding mechanistic conservation. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes this as inference from structural conservation data, while peer review treats it as part of the broader finding about Hsp90-Cdc37 client diversity.

Overlap on C6 regarding the 'hijacking' interpretation. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the term is interpretive but reasonable given structural conservation, while peer review affirms this as a major finding about pseudokinase-chaperone association.

Overlap on C67 regarding speculative regulatory mechanisms. OpenEval evaluates as UNCERTAIN, noting the model requires validation beyond structural data. Peer review evaluates as SUPPORTED, treating it as reasonable inference. Reflects different thresholds for speculative claims.

Overlap on C68-C69 regarding PP5 background and conflicting evidence. OpenEval evaluates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative nature of associated regulatory scenarios. Peer review evaluates as SUPPORTED, accepting these as appropriate context from prior work without challenge.

Overlap on C64 regarding evolutionary function speculation. OpenEval evaluates as UNCERTAIN, characterizing this as speculative inference. Peer review evaluates as SUPPORTED, treating it as part of the interpretive framework for understanding client diversity.

Overlap on C29-C31 regarding regulatory mechanisms background. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval treats these as established background with appropriate citations, while peer review affirms the pseudokinase-chaperone association finding that builds on this background.
